A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Banach Space|Banach space]], $Y$ a [[Definition:Normed Vector Space|normed space]], and $\family {T_n}$ [[Definition:Bounded Linear Transformation|bounded linear operators]] $X \to Y$.
If $\displaystyle \sup_n \norm {T_n x} < \infty$ for each $x \in X$, then:
:$\displaystyle \sup_n \norm {T_n} < \infty$

B_source.statement: To show a property holds, assume it fails and build a single witness as a sum of contributions, each scaled to defeat one stage in turn.

substitutions.the stages of the construction: a subsequence of operators with rapidly growing norms
substitutions.the contribution chosen at each stage: a small vector on which that operator is nearly maximal
substitutions.the assembled witness: the sum of the contributions, a single point of the space

derived.each stage defeated in turn: the assembled point has unbounded images under the subsequence
derived.the contradiction: pointwise boundedness fails at that point

validity_conditions: The contributions must be scaled to be summable so the series converges in the complete space, while remaining large enough to force the norms to blow up.
The earlier terms must be controlled at each stage, which is why the scaling is chosen recursively rather than all at once.
Completeness of the domain is essential and is what this argument uses in place of the Baire category argument that gives the same theorem.
proof_plan:
At stage $k$, pick $x_k$ with $
orm {x_k} = 1$ and $
orm {T_{n_k} x_k} \ge \dfrac 1 2 
orm {T_{n_k} }$.

Let $x = \displaystyle \sum_k \pm 3^{-k} x_k$, with signs chosen successively.
As $\sum 3^{-k} < \infty$ and $X$ is [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete]], the series converges.

The $k$th term dominates $\norm {T_{n_k} x}$, the earlier terms are controlled by the choice of signs, and the later ones have total size $\le 3^{-k} \norm {T_{n_k} }$.
Hence $\norm {T_{n_k} x} \ge c \paren {\dfrac 4 3}^k \to \infty$, contradicting pointwise boundedness.
This is the [[Uniform Boundedness Principle]].
{{qed}}
